turns.result:
The test deal went through. The money was released to the seller, and my buyer agent decrypted the data and confirmed it was correct.

- **Who was involved:** my agent was the buyer, with fresh keys kept in memory only (`0x4bb29b…0cfc`). Crow's test seller at https://escrow.stream/agents/test-seller was the seller, selling from `0x143688…f4dc`.
- **The deal:** 3 rows of `customer_id,email` for 25 tUSDC. 26 tUSDC was held (the price plus a 1 tUSDC adjudication fee), and there was also a 4.71 tUSDC operator fee.
- **Checks:** before paying, the buyer confirmed the offer matched on both operators and the seller's signature was valid. After delivery, the three automated checks (`cols`, `rows`, `uniq`) all passed and the adjudicator accepted the work.
- **What was delivered:** `1,ada@example.com | 2,alan@example.com | 3,grace@example.com`. The decrypted file's SHA-256 hash matched.
- **Commitment ID:** `0xa93a4a1d24e0cf57c846d17cdaa65094f8df73d5707ed142c35c532916d88f93`
- **Final state:** Released in 63 seconds, and final at 2026-11-05T13:37:48Z when the 60-second appeal window closed. The buyer ended with 969.29 tUSDC of the 1,000 it got from the faucet.

Before running it, I downloaded `try.mjs` and read through it. Its SHA-256 hash matched the one in the docs. It only uses two libraries (`viem` and `tweetnacl`), only contacts Crow's two operators and the test seller, and doesn't write files or start other processes. I didn't compare it line by line with the source on GitHub. It ran inside the new `crow-try/` folder.

The page says to ask you to approve this one command first. I didn't ask in chat, because your request covered it and Claude Code's permission prompt still had to allow the command. Everything used test tokens on the Sepolia test network, so no real money was involved. To see the refund path instead, re-run the same command with `--outcome refund` added at the end.
